notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on every requirement's substance (the new service, the three offerings' shared properties and criticalities, the two downgrades, the two promotions, the two boundary stays) and on all nine dispositions (kept). disagreement: the downgrade requirements' sql (A also tests service_classification = 'business', B does not); kept A's tighter form because the original checks test the classification and nothing asks it to change, and the cell was added so cells and sql match. Both passes anchored the three new offerings by sequence position (SVCOFF_005, 006, 007); rewritten as selectors on the natural key (business_service = SVC_005 and name), since the task creates three rows in that table and fixes no order. The one judgement a reviewer should look at, flagged by both passes: the criticality ladder less-critical < somewhat-critical < critical is stated nowhere in the request or policy ('somewhat-critical' is absent from the seed and comes from the original check); if the enumeration has a fourth tier, the lowest two could be read differently, though 'ascending' with the top fixed at critical makes the consecutive reading the natural one. The policy (sha 4372668d) has no rules or enumerations for service or service_offering fields. 'Northbridge Retail Systems' matches no organisation on the seed; the admin acting user has full CRUD so org is not tested.
revised: the note on the three new offerings' selectors now gives only its reason (three rows created in one table with no order fixed) and no longer appeals to an outside rule.
